Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-04-12 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Priya Raman (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Maya Li (Redwood CSM); Carlos Mendes (Nimbus Head of Search), Aisha Khan (ML Engineer), Tom Berger (Infra), Lena Ortiz (Product)

---
Summary (auto): quick demo of hosted embeddings + reranker with Q&A.
Topics: see metadata.

[00:00] Priya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Priya from Redwood. we have Ethan on the call to run through embeddings + our reranker flow, and Maya from CSM for next steps. how's everyone's afternoon?
[00:18] Carlos: good thanks, quick context — Nimbus search powers our customer portal and retention flows; we've seen a drop in click-through for knowledge base results, relevance is getting worse after recent content additions.
[00:32] Priya: got it, perfect. goal for today: show hosted embeddings API, how you can plug into your retriever and either run a Redwood rerank endpoint or use your vector DB + rerank, and then talk pilot.
[00:45] Ethan: yeah i'll demo calls from the console and the API, show latency numbers, and a small rerank example with typical 5-20 candidate pipeline.
[01:05] Aisha: quick Q up front — we use FAISS on k8s, and a hybrid of BM25 + embeddings. we're sensitive to 95th pct latency <120ms for web search. cost is also a big factor.
[01:22] Ethan: fair — we'll show two configs: low-latency mode (dedicated pooling/continuous batching off) and cost-optimized (batching, caching). note hosted will have different SLOs than Dedicated but it's usually good for pilots.
[01:40] Tom: also curious about data residency and encryption at rest — we need keys in our KMS if possible.
[01:51] Priya: yes we support customer-managed KMS for Private; for hosted we offer envelope encryption and are SOC 2 compliant — we'll share the security pack.

[05:10] Ethan: demo start — console view: here's the embeddings endpoint, model catalog — note the profile for the embedding model shows average vector dim 1536 and throughput for batch size 64. (screen share misc) [transcription: "screen share details fuzzy"]
[06:05] Ethan: example curl for embeddings: curl POST to /v1/embeddings with text payload. returns vector, then you index with FAISS or Typesense+vec. we recommend normalizing with L2 and using cosine for similarity.
[07:20] Carlos: any rate limits we should expect? we have spikes from search indexing job.
[07:30] Priya: hosted has quotas per account; we can allow burst for pilots. for production we recommend Dedicated if you need predictable throughput.

[09:40] Ethan: moving to rerank: typical flow we recommend — retrieve candidates via your vector DB or BM25, then call Redwood rerank endpoint with query + list of candidate texts+ids; reranker returns score and preferred ordering. advantage: reranker is model-aware and reduces false positives.
[10:12] Aisha: is rerank run on the same model that generated embeddings? will that cause data leakage or compounding?
[10:25] Ethan: good question — they can be different. embeddings model optimized for vector space, reranker is a cross-encoder; they operate on transient payloads unless you opt to store them. hosted does not persist request content beyond short logs unless configured.

[12:00] Priya: here's an example where we took Nimbus-style queries and ran baseline BM25 + embeddings retrieval vs embeddings + Redwood rerank. you can see lift in NDCG. (shared chart link: drive://nimbus-sample-results)
[12:42] Carlos: those numbers look promising, what's the token cost?
[12:50] Ethan: embeddings cost measured per 1k tokens for the text we encode; rerank cost is per candidate pair since cross-encoder scores query+doc; typical pilot low volume should be under your free credit but production cost depends on candidate count. we'll send a cost model sheet.

[16:05] Aisha: we do 50 candidates right now then shortlist to 5 in current pipeline — 50 would be expensive on rerank. any suggestions?
[16:18] Ethan: yes two patterns: 1) hybrid — use vector db to cut to 10-20, then rerank; 2) lightweight sparse retrieval + embed rerank. also batching reduces cost for embeddings. we have a feature called prefix/KV caching that speeds repeated user sessions. note: transcription may say "KV cache" as "K V cache"

[20:00] Tom: infra question — does hosted rerank require us to push text payloads through Redwood network? compliance folks will ask.
[20:12] Priya: hosted obviously routes through Redwood; if you need VPC/private we have Redwood Private or Dedicated with private peering options, and customer-managed KMS + audit logs, plus SOC2 report. we'll attach the SOC2 and network diagram.

[23:30] Ethan: quick live API call: I POSTed the rerank request with 8 candidates — see 95th pct latency ~180ms in hosted shared region, median 90ms. (note: these are demo env numbers)
[24:05] Carlos: 180ms is a hair over our 120ms bar for 95th. would Dedicated help?
[24:20] Ethan: Dedicated lowers variability; you'd get lower p95 predictable throughput. also you can tune model size (smaller reranker model) to shave latency with some quality tradeoff. We'll give recommendations and quant profiles.

[28:00] Aisha: curious about evaluation — can we run A/B with our current infra?
[28:12] Priya: yes, Redwood Console supports rollouts and canary, plus token-level cost dashboards and per-route latency. you can do a staged rollout: 10% of traffic to rerank and evaluate clicks/ctr.

[31:40] Ethan: showed console tracing demo — sample trace for request, token breakdown, and a folded view of per-host latency. (screen noise)
[33:00] Lena: what's the onboarding time to run a small pilot? we have half a sprint to prove lift.
[33:10] Priya: pilot can be run in 2-3 weeks if you provide sample logs and a small label set. SE will prepare the initial notebook to map your schema to the rerank call.

[35:20] Carlos: security followups — do you have SSO / SAML for console? we need RBAC so only search team can trigger rerank endpoints.
[35:33] Maya: yes SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, RBAC per team. also audit logs are available and we can set retention levels.

[37:55] Aisha: any gotchas with tokenization or weird characters in our KB? we have lots of code blocks and financial abbreviations.
[38:08] Ethan: tokenization differences can affect embedding length. we recommend pre-processing (strip code blocks or mark them) or using model-specific tokenizers; we'll share a sample preproc script.

[40:00] Tom: networking — does hosted support private peering?
[40:08] Priya: hosted doesn't by default; for private peering you look at Redwood Private or a hybrid with VPC endpoints. we'll map out options.

[42:30] Ethan: cost modeling notes — if you want a quick estimate, send typical monthly query volume, avg candidates per query, avg doc length. we'll return a cost projection including embedding + rerank costs and a Dedicated sizing suggestion.

[44:15] Carlos: ok this is useful. one last question — we use Pinecone for vector store, any limitations integrating with Redwood?
[44:25] Ethan: no; we integrate with any vector db. common pattern: store vectors in Pinecone/FAISS and call Redwood rerank. we did mention Pinecone earlier; no vendor lock.

[46:00] Priya: recap — we'll send: 1) hosted embeddings + rerank deck, 2) security pack (SOC2, KMS options), 3) pricing sheet + cost model, 4) small SE notebook + faiss example. Next step: Nimbus to share sample logs + label set and Priya/Ethan to schedule pilot kickoff.
[46:28] Carlos: sounds good, we'll aim to get logs to you this week.
[46:40] Priya: great, thanks all. we'll follow up with calendar invites and links to artifacts.
[46:50] Aisha: thanks everyone.
[47:00] (meeting ends)
